aptu-coder

A Model Context Protocol (MCP) code-intelligence server that gives AI coding agents pre-parsed symbol tables instead of raw file bytes, cutting token usage by up to 59% in the cited benchmark conditions (see Benchmarks). OpenSSF silver certified: fewer than 1% of open source projects reach this level.

> [!NOTE] > Native agent tools (regex search, path matching, file reading) handle targeted lookups well. `aptu-coder` handles the mechanical, non-AI work: mapping directory structure and extracting symbols, so a coding agent's context window is spent reasoning instead of re-deriving structure on every call. Most code-intelligence tooling for AI agents indexes a codebase into a cloud embedding or vector store and retrieves by similarity search. aptu-coder instead parses the codebase on-device with tree-sitter and serves it locally over MCP: no source code leaves the machine, and retrieval is exact (symbol tables) rather than approximate (nearest-neighbor similarity). ## Benchmarks Paired comprehension tasks on Claude Code (MCP mode vs native shell search). Methodology: [Django](https://github.com/django/django) auth migration ([v12](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/aptu-coder/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/v12/methodology.md)) and [OpenFAST](https://github.com/OpenFAST/openfast) AeroDyn integration audit ([v13](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/aptu-coder/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/v13/methodology.md)). | Task | Mode | Sonnet 4.6 | Haiku 4.5 | Savings | |---|---|---|---|---| | Django (Python) | MCP | 112k tokens, $0.39 | 406k tokens, $0.42 | **59% fewer tokens, 59% cheaper** (Sonnet) | | Django (Python) | Native | 276k tokens, $0.95 | 473k tokens, $0.53 | 14% fewer tokens, 21% cheaper (Haiku) | | OpenFAST (Fortran) | MCP | 472k tokens, $1.65 | 687k tokens, $0.72 | **46% fewer tokens, 42% cheaper** (Sonnet) | | OpenFAST (Fortran) | Native | 877k tokens, $2.85 | 2162k tokens, $2.21 | **68% fewer tokens, 68% cheaper** (Haiku) | A real end-to-end multi-agent run against this repository itself: five refactoring issues (#1578–#1582) fixed by the [coder skill](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/agentic-coder-skill) in one orchestrated session — 23 subagent spawns (5 scout, 1 guard, 10 build, 7 check), ~1h42m, three human interventions — producing PRs #1584–#1588, all merged with CI green. [Case study](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/agentic-coder-skill/blob/main/docs/examples/2026-09-aptu-coder-5-issues.md). ### Scope of the benchmark claims The token-savings figures above come from single, focused comprehension tasks where the agent used aptu-coder instead of shell search. Agentic coding loops have bash and ripgrep and can search the repo directly. The [v19 benchmark program](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/aptu-coder/blob/main/docs/audit/2026-09-30-v19-pivot.md) (N=20 paired sessions, pre-registered claim gate) measured aptu-coder in those loops: no measurable answer-quality gain over bash + ripgrep on structural fan-in tasks (pooled paired F1 diff mean -0.071, 95% CI [-0.179, +0.038]; gate NOT-SUPPORTED); tool activation itself was reliable when tools were surfaced directly. {"body":"## Summary

Add PHP language support to aptu-coder using the official `tree-sitter-php` grammar. After this change, `analyze_directory`, `analyze_file` and `analyze_module` extract functions, methods, classes, interfaces, traits, enums, calls, imports and inheritance from `.php` files instead of returning the unsupported-extension fallback.

## Context

- PHP is one of the most widely deployed server-side languages and is absent from the registry: no `php` in `EXTENSION_MAP` (`crates/aptu-coder-core/src/lang.rs`), no handler in `crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/`, no `tree-sitter-php` in `Cargo.lock`.
- aptu-coder already supports mainstream languages such as Java, Kotlin, Swift and TypeScript. PHP should follow the same registry pattern as the existing object-oriented languages.

## Prerequisites

None.

## Where to Look

- **Handler templates:** `crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/java.rs` (an OO language with `extends` / `implements`) and `swift.rs` (inheritance through named children, inline tests).
- **Grammar:** the `tree-sitter-php` repository on GitHub. Node kinds and field names come from `php/src/node-types.json`; the crate entry points are on docs.rs.
- **Registry:** `languages/mod.rs` (handler registration) and `lang.rs` (extension map and supported-language list).

## Scope

- A new handler, `crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/php.rs`, with the SPDX header and the five query constants used by the other handlers (`ELEMENT_QUERY`, `CALL_QUERY`, `REFERENCE_QUERY`, `IMPORT_QUERY`, `DEFUSE_QUERY`).
- An `extract_inheritance` handler with the same contract as the Java handler.
- Registry wiring for `"php"` in both `languages/mod.rs` and `lang.rs`.
- Unit tests in `php.rs` and one integration test file under `crates/aptu-coder/tests/`.
- `README.md`: add PHP to the Supported Languages list and the intro count.

You choose the crate version, the node kinds and fields, the query text, the grammar entry point and the handler slots to wire. The crate must clear `cargo deny`'s package age check without `SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK`.

## Suggested Approach

1. Pick the crate version from crates.io and check it against the workspace `tree-sitter` version.
2. Parse a small sample `.php` file with the grammar and list the node kinds and fields you see. Confirm each one in `php/src/node-types.json` before you use it.
3. Write the five queries and prove they compile in a unit test before wiring anything. The tree-sitter query syntax documentation covers captures and fields.
4. Mirror the registry wiring of the most recent language addition.
5. Add the unit tests and the integration test last.

Expect a day or two of work; most of it is step 2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tree-sitter-php` is declared in the root `[workspace.dependencies]` and in `crates/aptu-coder-core/Cargo.toml`; `Cargo.lock` is updated; `cargo deny check advisories licenses bans` passes without `SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK`
- [ ] `crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/php.rs` exists with the SPDX header, the five query constants and `extract_inheritance`
- [ ] `php` is in `EXTENSION_MAP` and in `supported_languages()` in `lang.rs`
- [ ] `"php"` is wired into `get_language_info()` and `get_ts_language()` in `languages/mod.rs`
- [ ] `analyze_file` on a `.php` file returns `language: "php"` and lists functions, methods, class / interface / trait / enum declarations, free, `->` and `::` calls, and `use` imports
- [ ] `analyze_module` on the same file returns the same element set; `analyze_directory` labels it `php`
- [ ] `extract_inheritance` on `class Foo extends Bar implements A, B` returns `["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"]`; on a class with no clauses it returns `[]`
- [ ] A `.php` file that mixes HTML and `<?php ... ?>` parses with zero ERROR nodes and yields the same PHP elements as the PHP-only equivalent
- [ ] Unit tests in `php.rs` cover: the queries compile, the element query matches a class and a function, the inheritance happy path and the no-clause edge case
- [ ] An integration test covers one happy path and the HTML-template edge case, using `common::call_tool_raw` and `tempfile::NamedTempFile` as in `tests/integration_tests.rs`
- [ ] `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass
- [ ] REUSE compliance passes; the binary size delta is stated in the PR description
- [ ] Commits are GPG signed and DCO signed off

## Not in Scope

- `extract_function_name`, `find_method_for_receiver`, `find_receiver_type` (no consumer since #1807)
- Trait `use` resolution, property and constant extraction, attributes, namespace import aliasing
- `.phtml`, `.inc`, `.module`, `.php5` extensions
- Tool handler or schema changes; other languages

## Note on Process

The maintainers are implementing this in-house. External pull requests for this issue are not being accepted at this time and will be closed.

## Related

- #648 and #1742: the Swift integration, the most recent language addition
- #1063: binary size delta reporting

## Commit Message Format

We follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format:

```
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body>

<footer>
```

### Types

- **feat**: A new feature
- **fix**: A bug fix
- **docs**: Documentation only changes
- **refactor**: A code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
- **test**: Adding missing tests or correcting existing tests
- **chore**: Changes to build process, dependencies, or tooling

### Examples

```bash
# Feature with scope
git commit -S --signoff -m "feat(analysis): add support for TypeScript generics"

# Bug fix
git commit -S --signoff -m "fix: handle empty source files without panicking"

# Breaking change
git commit -S --signoff -m "feat!: redesign tool parameter schema

BREAKING CHANGE: The path parameter is now required"

# Documentation
git commit -S --signoff -m "docs: update tool descriptions in README"
```

## Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO)

All commits must be signed off to certify you have the right to submit the code:

```bash
git commit -S --signoff -m "Your commit message"
```

This adds `Signed-off-by: Your Name <email>` to your commit, certifying you agree to the [DCO](https://developercertificate.org/).

# Copilot Instructions

## Assigning issues to Copilot

REST API method:
```
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number} --method PATCH -f "assignees[]=copilot-swe-agent[bot]"
```
UI method: use the issue sidebar to assign to `copilot-swe-agent[bot]`.

## PR iteration

- Comment `@copilot` with specific feedback; agent pushes follow-up commits
- If unresolved after 2 iterations: close PR, amend issue, re-assign

## Copilot code review

Flag:
- Hallucinated APIs; verify against `Cargo.lock` and `cargo doc --open`
- Scope creep beyond the issue deliverables
- Missing error handling
- rmcp, tree-sitter, schemars version assumptions; verify against installed versions
- Missing `cargo deny check advisories licenses` run when `Cargo.toml` changes
- New dependency added without justification in the PR description
- `working_dir` outside the server CWD boundary accepted without error (must be rejected with INVALID_PARAMS)
- Profile-based tool routing (`APTU_CODER_PROFILE` / `io.clouatre-labs/profile`) bypassed or ignored in tools/list
- `gh release create` used instead of `git tag -s vX.Y.Z -m "vX.Y.Z"`
- Tool descriptions or server instructions reference host-specific clients (e.g. "Claude Code", "Cursor")
- Commit missing GPG signature or DCO sign-off (`-S --signoff`)

## Design references

- [ARCHITECTURE.md](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) - design, language handlers, "How to add a language"
- [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) - project conventions and implementation status

## Firewall

- Copilot runs in a firewalled GitHub Actions environment; no arbitrary URLs
- If a build step needs a URL not in the allow list, document it in the PR
- Maintainer updates `.github/copilot/firewall.yml`

New language handlers must register all fields in `src/languages/mod.rs` `get_language_info()`. Flag a new language file in `src/languages/` that is not matched by a new arm in the `get_language_info` match block.

## tree-sitter query strings

- Queries must use named captures (`@func_name`, `@call`, `@import_path`). Flag positional-only captures.
- `IMPL_TRAIT_QUERY` must only match `(type_identifier)` for the trait name -- scoped traits (`impl io::Sink for T`) are intentionally out of scope. Flag attempts to extend it to `scoped_type_identifier`.

## Handler function signatures

All four handler function types must match the type aliases in `src/languages/mod.rs`:

- `ExtractFunctionNameHandler`: `fn(&Node, &str, &str) -> Option<String>`
- `FindMethodForReceiverHandler`: `fn(&Node, &str, Option<usize>) -> Option<String>`
- `FindReceiverTypeHandler`: `fn(&Node, &str) -> Option<String>`
- `ExtractInheritanceHandler`: `fn(&Node, &str) -> Vec<String>`

Flag handler functions with signatures that deviate from these types.

## Optional fields

`reference_query`, `import_query`, `impl_query`, `impl_trait_query` are `Option<&'static str>`. Use `None` for languages that do not support the concept. Flag `Some("")` (empty string) as a substitute for `None`.

## Kotlin-specific notes

Kotlin registers two extensions: `.kt` (source) and `.kts` (script). Both map to the same `LanguageInfo` entry. When writing Kotlin tree-sitter queries, note that `.kts` files may contain top-level expressions that `.kt` source files do not; queries should not assume a class or object wrapper is always present.

## Structure

- One happy path and one edge case per distinct behavior. Flag test files where multiple tests exercise the same code path with only input variation (e.g., testing the same parse logic for five different languages when one representative suffices).

- Use `TempDir` from the `tempfile` crate for filesystem fixtures. Flag tests that write to hardcoded paths, and avoid introducing new uses of `std::env::temp_dir()` directly.

## Assertions

- Prefer specific assertions over boolean ones: `assert_eq!(output.functions.len(), 2)` over `assert!(output.functions.len() > 0)`. Flag `assert!(x > 0)` when an exact count is knowable from the fixture.
- Assert on the property under test, not on implementation details. Flag assertions that check internal field names or intermediate struct layouts that are not part of the public API.

## Async tests

- Use `#[tokio::test]` for async test functions. Flag `#[test]` on functions that call `.await`.

## Fixtures

- Inline fixture source as a raw string literal (`r#"..."#`) for small cases. Flag test files that read fixture data from external files under `tests/` unless the fixture is reused across three or more test functions.
- Shared fixtures belong in `tests/fixtures.rs`. Flag duplicate fixture definitions across test files.

- Test files must not contain `#[allow(dead_code)]` suppressing unused fixture helpers. Flag it: the helper should be removed or moved to `fixtures.rs`.
- Do not introduce new `use aptu_coder::*` glob imports in test files; if you touch an existing glob import, replace it with explicit imports so it is clear what is under test.

content.text:
### Alternation with captures for function and method

Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/blob/master/docs/src/using-parsers/queries/2-operators.md

Matches a call to either a variable or an object property, capturing the variable as @function and the property as @method.

```query
(call_expression
  function: [
    (identifier) @function
    (member_expression
      property: (property_identifier) @method)
  ])
```

--------------------------------

### Query Syntax > Fields

Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/blob/master/docs/src/using-parsers/queries/1-syntax.md

In general, it's a good idea to make patterns more specific by specifying [field names][node-field-names] associated with
child nodes. You do this by prefixing a child pattern with a field name followed by a colon. For example, this pattern would
match an `assignment_expression` node where the `left` child is a `member_expression` whose `object` is a `call_expression`.

```query
(assignment_expression
  left: (member_expression
    object: (call_expression)))
```

--------------------------------

### Operators > Capturing Nodes

Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/blob/master/docs/src/using-parsers/queries/2-operators.md

When matching patterns, you may want to process specific nodes within the pattern. Captures allow you to associate names
with specific nodes in a pattern, so that you can later refer to those nodes by those names. Capture names are written _after_
the nodes that they refer to, and start with an `@` character.

For example, this pattern would match any assignment of a `function` to an `identifier`, and it would associate the name
`the-function-name` with the identifier:

```query
(assignment_expression
  left: (identifier) @the-function-name
  right: (function))
```

And this pattern would match all method definitions, associating the name `the-method-name` with the method name, `the-class-name`
with the containing class name:

```query
(class_declaration
  name: (identifier) @the-class-name
  body: (class_body
    (method_definition
      name: (property_identifier) @the-method-name)))
```

--------------------------------

### Pattern with field names for assignment_expression

Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/blob/master/docs/src/using-parsers/queries/1-syntax.md

Matches an assignment_expression where the left child is a member_expression whose object is a call_expression. Field names are prefixed with a colon.

```query
(assignment_expression
  left: (member_expression
    object: (call_expression)))
```

--------------------------------

### Alternation without quantifiers

Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/blob/master/docs/src/using-parsers/queries/2-operators.md

Shows an alternation without quantifiers, producing four matches each with one capture. Includes regex equivalent.

```query
[
  (preproc_include)
  (comment)
] @capture
; ^ Produces four matches, each with one capture:
; [
;   "#include <foo>\n",
; ],
; [
;   "#include <bar>\n",
; ],
; [
;   "#include <baz>\n",
; ],
; [
;   "// comment",
; ]
;
; Regex equivalent: [ab]
```

**Recommendation: Approach A, the issue-literal registry parity.** Add `languages/php.rs` with the five query constants and a kind-based `extract_inheritance`, modelled on `java.rs` and `swift.rs`. Pin `tree-sitter-php` 0.25.2 and use `LANGUAGE_PHP`. Wire it the way `css` is wired: `Cargo.toml` (root and core), `Cargo.lock`, `EXTENSION_MAP`, `supported_languages()`, `pub mod`, both `get_language_info`/`get_ts_language` arms, the registry test table, an integration test, and the README. Approach B adds receiver handlers the issue excludes. Approach C drops `DEFUSE_QUERY` and omits `enum_declaration`, which the upstream `tags.scm` lacks.

**Findings that matter for the plan:**
- **`DEFUSE_QUERY` is not compiler-required.** `defuse_query` is `Option<&str>`, and `parser.rs` treats `None` as "no defuse". It is required by the issue's five-constant scope and acceptance criteria, and by the test-coverage convention in `parser.rs` line 80. The output says this explicitly, so the premise is corrected rather than accepted as stated.
- **PHP variables include the `$`.** `variable_name` text includes the dollar sign, and defuse matching is exact text equality. Callers must pass `$x`, unlike Java identifiers.
- **Inheritance has no field names.** `base_clause` and `class_interface_clause` are reached by child kind. Their named children are `name`, `qualified_name`, and `relative_name`, as in Swift.
- **Imports hit the generic fallback.** `extract_imports_from_node` has no PHP arm, so import text comes through the fallback branch.
- **Package age.** `tree-sitter-php` v0.25.2 was published 2026-11-19, which is about 8 to 9 days old. v0.25.1 is the fallback. I could not confirm the crates.io publish date from here.

- The queries were checked against `node-types.json` and `grammar.json` but never compiled. The first `cargo test` is the real check.
- `gh api` returned an "outside the experiment's fence" message for the issue REST endpoint. The issue body was read through `gh issue view` with `-R` instead, and the grammar files were read through `gh api`.
